_comment: Bean sfhr. The three defects the bean names (70c7 empty body, 52dz folded title, nvbr blocked on a scrapped bean) plus the five the same readers found beside them, as they stood on 2026-09-20. sfhr is explicit that these are repaired BY THEIR OWNERS and that the bean does not edit them, so the check lists them and fails only on a NEW one. Remove an entry when its bean is repaired; check-bean-bodies reports an entry that no longer matches as stale, so the baseline shrinks rather than fossilises. 2026-09-21, bean sfhr again: the shadow-checklist reader added five more, each an OPEN bean whose canonical Done-when reads unticked while a copy below it reads ticked — 0hi8, 81t5, ivfw, jbx2, xgd8. Same rule: their owners repair them, the check fails only on a new one. b963 is NOT baselined: it had the same defect and it is this session's own bean, so it was ticked in place instead. 2026-09-21, second pass: the reader learned that a `---` horizontal rule ends the canonical section too — 61 beans use one where 141 use a heading, and it had been folding their later checklist back INTO the canonical section, blind to all 61 while reporting them clean. That found three more, all in this session's own epic: cvab and sfhr were repaired in place, and oh78 is baselined because it is queued next here and not yet claimed — repairing an unclaimed bean is the thing bean-coordination cautions against. oh78 was removed from the baseline the moment it was claimed and repaired in place — a baseline entry is a deferral, not a home.
